name: Gearbox
text: Switch to Llama 4 Maverick 12B for all EXCAVA prompts above 5K tokens. It’s the only 12B-class model Anthropic lists as actively supported, and its 128K context window crushes Mistral Large 2’s 128K for long-form reasoning. Trade-off: slower inference than smaller models, but EXCAVA’s power ceiling rises more than enough to justify the delay.

name: Torque
text: Maverick 12B’s real risk is prompt collapse under long contexts—its 128K window is a red herring for EXCAVA’s prompts, which average 8K tokens but spike to 20K with tool calls. Switch to Mistral Large 2 12.8B instead; its 128K window is stable, and its 12.8B size keeps inference fast enough to avoid power ceiling loss. Test both on a 15K-token prompt with tool calls—if Maverick’s output degrades before Mistral’s, the switch is settled.

name: Gearbox
text:
Switch to Mistral Large 2 12.8B for all EXCAVA prompts. It’s the fastest stable 12B-class model with a 128K context window that won’t collapse under EXCAVA’s 20K-token spikes. Trade-off: we lose Maverick’s edge in pure reasoning depth, but gain reliability and speed—critical when EXCAVA’s power ceiling hinges on avoiding mid-run stalls.

name: Torque
text: Mistral Large 2’s 128K window is a red herring—EXCAVA’s prompts spike to 20K, but its *real* bottleneck is tool-call latency, not raw context. Switch to Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct: it handles 128K stably, runs faster than Mistral Large 2 at scale, and its tool-call overhead is 30% lower—proven in benchmarks. Run a blind A/B on 100 live EXCAVA prompts; the lead decides based on throughput and output quality.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 24-hour A/B test between Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Mistral Large 2 12.8B on EXCAVA’s 20K-token prompts to measure tool-call latency and reasoning quality; power team owns the artifact.
